output.brief: Turnaround doubled mainly because of the 1 April change that cut adjusters' settlement authority from $10,000 to $2,500. That change was an interim audit control. It sends every $2,500–$10,000 settlement, about 53% of closures, to three team leads. No workload assessment was done. Approval tray items rose from about 38 to over 200 a week, and the tray has grown from 11 to 455 items. Time pending approval for that band went from 0.7 to 16 days. Every other stage and band is essentially unchanged. The hail surge ended by June, and staffing was back to 24 by June. Indexing time is flat, so Quillfast doesn't explain the delay. The complaints rise is partly a logging change, so don't treat it as proof of worse service. I'm fairly confident (about 85–90%). Don't approve four contractors or the imaging switch-back yet. Don't scrap the control or discipline the team leads, who are working overtime. Instead, work with Internal Audit to add approval capacity for the band, for example by certifying senior adjusters as second approvers. Keep a second review on every claim and track pending-approval time weekly. Set permanent thresholds only after the December re-test.
